ai.description: Giri’s Geckoella reaches 50 mm in snout-vent length. It is brown with distinct white-edged dark crossbands and yellow spots. Distinguishing features include a slender body and granular dorsal scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus varadgirii* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, white-spotted dark nuchal collar and a lack of dark transverse bands on its dorsal body.
ai.habitat: *Cyrtodactylus varadgirii* inhabits the leaf litter of moist deciduous forests in the Northern Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 400 and 600 meters.
ai.behavior: Giri’s Geckoella is a strictly nocturnal hunter that remains hidden under leaf litter or rocks during the day to avoid predators and desiccation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtodactylus varadgirii* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: Cyrtodactylus varadgirii is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in Maharashtra, India, typically found in rocky habitats at elevations between 400 and 1,200 meters.
